courseName: MGT 867: Money, Power, and Purpose — Philanthropy in a Changing World

definitions.attendanceAndParticipation: Worth 40% — a significant fraction of the grade. The course requires substantial reading. Visiting guests from the field of philanthropy attend most sessions, and it is essential that students are well-prepared for and actively engage in those conversations. Academic integrity extends to participation: it is obvious to peers and instructors when you are multitasking, and if you cannot be fully present for the duration of the seminar each week you should not select this elective.
definitions.assignment1PartOneReflection: Worth 15%. A 2-3 page individual reflection (max 1,000 words) due Sunday September 27 by 11:59pm, responding to the prompt: consider a specific philanthropist or philanthropic organization, describe how themes from the first section of the course apply to their giving strategy, and recommend shifts to their approach.
definitions.assignment2AreasForInvestment: Worth 5%. A 1-2 page draft of your final project focus area(s), due Sunday November 8 by 11:59pm. Outline the primary area for investment and the rationale for that choice, plus the guiding principles or values for giving. These proposals may be discussed in class.
definitions.assignment3CaseVideos: Worth 10%. Over the semester you choose TWO cases to respond to individually through a short video reflection. Each video is a maximum of three minutes and focuses on your key takeaways from the case, guided by the discussion questions provided in the syllabus. Record with Zoom or any simple platform; reflections should be thoughtful but need not be polished or heavily produced. Videos are due by 11:59pm on the Wednesday before the class session in which the case will be discussed. Eligible cases are marked in the syllabus with '{Case reflection video opportunity}'.
definitions.assignment4FinalProject: Worth 30%. A team-based project (groups of up to four) in which you advise a high-net-worth individual on a strategy for their $100M set aside for philanthropy. Each group selects one donor profile from pre-developed cases. Two parts: a maximum 6-8 minute video pitch due December 4, and a final memo (max 8 pages double-spaced, ~2,000 words) summarizing the pitch. Both are directed to your donor. The memo can be submitted with the video pitch, or after the final class discussion if you want to fine-tune based on feedback — in which case it is due no later than 11:59pm on December 21. The pitch must advise on: sector(s) to impact, model of philanthropy and why, organizational form (LLC, 501(c)(3), etc.), guiding principles and decision-making criteria, percentage allocations across investment types, at least one key investment in each area, and how the design addresses critiques of today's philanthropy, particularly regarding race and power.
definitions.devicePolicy: We are analog in the classroom — no laptops, phones, or other electronic devices during class. Pen and paper are provided for anyone who doesn't carry them. There is a break between the two sessions if you need to check your phone.
definitions.aiPolicy: All submitted work must be your own; language, data, and ideas from other sources must be documented. Use of ChatGPT or other AI composition software is discouraged, but if you use it you must share the prompt you used to generate the response.

gradingPolicy: Attendance and Participation: 40%; Assignment 1: Part 1 Reflection: 15%; Assignment 2: Areas for Investment and Guiding Principles: 5%; Assignment 3: 2 Case Videos: 10%; Assignment 4: Final Project Video and Memo: 30%.
